page: Google Cloud Platform n4a-standard-2 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on 64-bit ARM architecture. The instance is provisioned with 2 dedicated Neoverse-N3 physical cores from the ARMv8 family, operating at a base frequency of 3.4 GHz with 1 thread per core. Memory allocation totals 8.0 GB, establishing a standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The cache structure provides 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 112 MB L3 cache. Cryptographic processing is accelerated via hardware-supported AES instructions, while vector instruction extensions such as AVX and AMX are absent. The instance does not bundle local NVMe storage or GPU accelerators, relying on network-attached storage for persistent file systems.

Performance benchmarks reflect the modest capacity of a dual-core configuration. Single-threaded gzip compression achieves strong throughput at 32.69 GB/sec, placing it within the top 25 percent of tested systems. Single-core compute on stress-ng scores 2058.78, indicating average baseline core execution. Uncached large-block memory writes demonstrate average speeds of 36.72 GB/sec, while uncached reads register at 36.91 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-core stress-ng scores (4086.82) and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression throughput (18.69 GB/sec) rank in the lower performance brackets, limited by the dual-core boundary. Cached small-block memory bandwidth is similarly constrained at 141.61 GB/sec, and static web serving throughput measures at a modest 5.09 GB/sec.

From an operational efficiency perspective, the n4a-standard-2 delivers dedicated physical cores on ARM silicon, avoiding the resource contention common in burstable or shared-core tiers. While aggregate throughput is constrained by the physical core count, per-core execution stability remains consistent. The instance is best suited for entry-level production microservices, lightweight web serving, background queue consumers, CI/CD worker nodes, and small container runtimes that do not require high parallel throughput or dense local I/O.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4a-standard-2 is an entry-tier general-purpose instance powered by the arm64 architecture. Configured with 2 dedicated Neoverse-N3 physical cores running at a 3.4 GHz clock speed, it delivers 8.0 GB of memory at a balanced 1:4 core-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The processor includes 64 KB L1 data cache, 2 MB L2 cache, 112 MB L3 cache, and integrated AES hardware acceleration, while omitting local storage and GPU accelerators. Benchmark evaluations show strong single-threaded gzip compression performance alongside average single-core CPU throughput and uncached memory write bandwidth. However, overall multi-core computation, multi-threaded decompression, and cached memory throughput fall into lower benchmark percentiles due to the two-core footprint. Qualitative cost efficiency is favorable for applications leveraging efficient ARM silicon without demanding heavy parallel processing. The instance is suited for lightweight microservices, basic web serving, utility tasks, and development environments.
